findings: Solved 2026-10-30 on the owner's request (exercises book by book, in Practice): Chapter 16 (Identifying Hazards and Designing Safe Experiments) exercise as printed on PDF 348-349 (printed pages 348-349), in the book's words and order. Quick Check 16.4 on p348 above the exercise is not part of it.
Counts: Q.1 seven MCQs (I-VII); Q.2 eleven short questions a-k; Descriptive Q.3-Q.6 four questions. All solved in English and Roman Urdu.
No answer key is printed. MCQ keys: I c, II b, III d, IV c, V c, VI c, VII b.

Book correction, MCQ I option (c): 'lower meniscus does not exist for colored liquids' is loosely worded (the lower meniscus exists but cannot be seen through a dark liquid); keyed (c) as the intended answer with a Book correction box. Doubtful: a reviewer may prefer to keep only the explanation.

Many questions go beyond the chapter, which gives only the titration procedure, the indicating tests and the first-aid table: MCQ I (meniscus), II and Short a-c (indicator ranges, pKa), VI and VII (chromyl chloride and brown ring tests), Short d, g, i, j, k (dilute solutions, Ca(OH)2 solubility, diluting acids, carbonate hydrolysis, NaOH + CO2), Short h (vinegar titration method; no data invented), Q.5 and Q.6 confirmatory tests and excess-reagent reactions (MgSO4, chromyl chloride, brown ring, lead acetate, lake test, K4[Fe(CN)6], KSCN). All labelled '(beyond the chapter)'.
Short e: the chapter does not say that Al(OH)3 dissolves in excess NaOH; the answer states it (beyond the chapter) because it is needed to tell Al3+ from Ca2+.

Q.4 uses the chapter's corrected matching of Table 16.1 burns (five kinds printed, four treatments); a Roman Urdu Wazahat box explains, with blister care marked beyond the chapter. Q.5 nitrate: chapter's 'Al acts as a cathode' corrected (reducing agent) in a Wazahat box.
MCQ IV: the chapter describes Fe2+ with aqueous ammonia as a 'white gelatinous' Fe(OH)2 turning red-brown (with NaOH: green turning orange-brown); the question's green-then-brown fits Fe2+.
Comparison answers (Short e, Short f, Q.3) carry answer tables. No figures. Draft for the academic review.
